about: Sections of a competitor brief, in the order they appear. The report script knows each id; you may change the order and the titles, but every id must appear exactly once.

sections.title: Product identity
sections.purpose: What the product is and for whom, in two or three sentences, citing a fetched page from the product's own site. The name, site and how it was identified are shown too.

sections.title: Jobs to be done
sections.purpose: 3-5 jobs the product does for its users, each with a one-line reason and the pages that show it. A job with no fetched source is labelled inferred, no source.

sections.title: Features
sections.purpose: Table of name, description, build complexity (S/M/L/XL), how core it is (1-5) and the fetched page that shows it. A feature without a fetched source is dropped.

sections.title: Voice of customer
sections.purpose: Customer quotes copied word for word, with sentiment, the fetched page and the retrieval date. A quote without a fetched source is dropped.

sections.title: Gaps
sections.purpose: 3-7 weaknesses with a severity (low, medium or high) and the pages that show them. A gap with no fetched source is labelled inferred, no source.

sections.title: Opportunities
sections.purpose: 3-5 openings, each citing the gap or feature rows it builds on (G1, F2, ...) or fetched pages.

sections.title: Source attribution log
sections.purpose: Every page recorded in the run: fetched, not fetched, and any record the URL check refuses, plus every dropped row and ignored cite.
